prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules redirect the ubiquitin-proteasome system to eliminate proteins, from heterobifunctional degraders to the cereblon mechanism of molecular glues

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B036) to targeted protein degradation (B054) with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. Degraders are a molecular-design principle of the kind I value most: a bifunctional or glue-type small molecule brings an E3 ligase and a target together and turns drug action from occupancy into event-driven chemistry. The mechanism is supported by structures, ternary-complex kinetics and degradation measurements, and the cereblon work answered the old question of how thalidomide acts. It also changes what chemists and clinicians can do, since proteins once considered undruggable become reachable, and lenalidomide-class glues are already in routine clinical use, with heterobifunctional degraders in late-stage trials. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the heterobifunctional concept, and Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, so the citation can be tied to two traceable steps rather than to a diffuse field. B054 is also the ballot most often named across the round-1 files, so it is the place where scientific judgment and breadth of support currently overlap.
statement.case_against: No heterobifunctional degrader is approved yet, so some of the therapeutic payoff is still prospective, and the committee must accept that the glue strand carries the clinical record while the PROTAC strand carries the concept. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Ito, Gray and Kim are left out of a three-person cut, and Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and Ito's cereblon work are close to decisive for the field to become practical. A citation that spans two lineages may read as broader than a single clearly attributable discovery. Finally, B036 remains the stronger case on clinical scale, and I am setting it aside largely because of attribution, not because I doubt the science.

responses.point: Brzezinski asks for a single-part B054 prize with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, keeping the PROTAC concept and the cereblon glue mechanism in one citation, and concedes that credit is split across lineages and no PROTAC is yet approved.
responses.response: After round 1 I have moved to your configuration, not for convenience but because the credit chain is more traceable than in delivery chemistry: Crews and Deshaies for the heterobifunctional concept, Handa for the cereblon target. I agree the two strands belong in one citation, because both rest on the same principle of induced proximity to the ubiquitin-proteasome system, and the thalidomide mechanism gives the glue strand the clinical record that the PROTAC strand still lacks. I would resist narrowing to the concept alone, since that would leave the only approved drugs outside the citation. Where I remain uneasy is that Ciulli and Ito are left out, and I think the committee should say openly that the citation is tied to the principle and not to every contributor.

responses.point: Chabes pairs Liu alone for base editing with Crews and Deshaies alone for heterobifunctional degraders, and answered my B036 case by saying the attribution is too hard to defend and that the 2023 Medicine citation covers the same therapeutic story.
responses.response: I accept your point on B036 and it moved me: six names with decisive claims and industrial optimization cannot be cut to three without an arbitrary choice. On the prize shape I differ. I do not think a two-part prize joining base editing and degraders is the stronger unit, since you concede it may be weaker and that Komor and Gaudelli would have no room, and the clinical and safety record for base editing is still short. Within B054 I would keep Handa and not limit to Crews and Deshaies, because cereblon is the mechanistic basis of the molecular glues and a heterobifunctional-only citation would not explain thalidomide. I still support Liu alone as the defensible cut if base editing is considered, and I keep B069 as an alternative.

responses.point: Aqvist told me that the impact of LNPs is undeniable but that attribution across six names is the difficulty, and that he would not accept the three most prominent names as a settlement, while his own preference is Car and Parrinello and his B054 allocation uses Ciulli rather than Handa.
responses.response: You were right, and I could not produce the defensible trio you asked for, so I am no longer proposing B036 as my first choice. On B054 we differ on Handa against Ciulli. I keep Handa because cereblon explained thalidomide and underpins the glues with the longest clinical record, whereas Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands are a technical step that made PROTACs practical. I would accept a Ciulli allocation as defensible if the committee prefers a more structural-chemistry emphasis. I respect the clean credit of B059, but I still read it as a methods prize with narrower reach, and I will not rank it above B054.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, supports B017 with Miyasaka, Snaith and Park and notes that B054 appears in five top-three lists, that credit in B017 is contested, and that operational stability and lead content are unresolved.
responses.response: Your chair summary question about whether absence of an approved PROTAC delays recognition is the one that matters most to me. My answer is that the cereblon glues already provide approved clinical proof of the principle, so the discovery is mature in the sense I care about. I see the same attribution difficulty in B017 that you do, and your own cut and Zou's are identical, which is a point in its favor, but I weigh the unresolved stability and lead issues more heavily than you do. I would not call B017 premature as a discovery, only less clearly settled for a prize this year than degraders.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can write one citation that credits both the heterobifunctional concept and the cereblon glue mechanism without it reading as two discoveries.
Whether Handa or Ciulli (or Ito or Sakamoto) is the better third name, which I cannot settle from priority records in the files.
Whether the absence of an approved heterobifunctional degrader should delay recognition for one more cycle.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal need for any shortlisted candidate. My research overlaps with Emma Sparr's in peptide-lipid and self-assembly systems, which touches B036 and B044 only as a field overlap. My postdoc mentors (Stevens, Boey) are not credited on any shortlisted ballot. This disclosure is unchanged from round 1.
